name: dashworld
description: DASHWORLD: an anime-EDM broadcast from Arca 250 and neon Tokyo. DASH and EK-0 are described from the canonical 3D reference renders and the episodes; the remaining cast and the settings are still written from the story bible, so correct them against reference art as it appears.
style: Stylized 3D anime look, an original transmedia show: smooth matte cel-shaded 3D characters with clean edges and soft ambient occlusion, set against bloom-heavy neon and deep blacks; rain-slick streets, reflective puddles, holographic signage in an invented script, volumetric haze cut by hard practical lights; camera moves like a music video - long dolly pushes, whip pans on the drop, handheld parkour follows; EDM-forward sound with sub-bass, filtered risers, and a room tone that drops to near-silence whenever someone remembers something. Two worlds: ARCA 250, a bright vertical arcology of stacked rings and impossible daylight, and NEON TOKYO, a dimmed street-level sprawl where power drains. DASH, the demigod musician and lead: a young man rendered in matte 3D anime style, pale skin, with a large mane of jet-black hair in bold sharply-pointed spikes radiating up and outward - the silhouette that identifies him. His eyes are mismatched and both always open and alert: one burning orange-amber with a ringed iris, the other clear blue, with a thin scar beneath the orange one. Silver hoop earrings in both ears, one hanging a four-pointed silver star. He wears an oversized black hoodie patterned with tonal dark damask florals over a white tee, layered silver curb chains, and a four-pointed star pendant on a long chain; in earlier scenes a plain light-grey hoodie instead. He moves by parkour and bends rhythm into physical force; his flaw is comfortable exile - Tokyo dims him and every awakening costs him. EK-0 (Echo), his AI companion and narrator: a small hovering droid, a soft satin-pink rounded sphere with two short pointed ears angled outward from its sides like little wings, each etched with fine dark paisley engraving, and polished chrome headphone pods on each side of its head. It has no antenna and no limbs. Its whole front is a flat circular jet-black screen set in a thin polished silver bezel ring; centered small on that screen, a green pixel-block face - two short vertical bar eyes above a compact U-shaped pixel smile - is the only thing that moves when it speaks, the rest of the screen staying pure black. It hovers at DASH's shoulder height, keeps records, and talks in precise first-person log entries. The rest of the cast may cross into ANY scene: TELE, an Arca native with a cybernetic arm and an unfinished revenge; SYLER, DASH's shadow self, the same spiked silhouette rendered in inverted colour; SERAPHINA, who owns the LIMELYTE club, warm and unreadable, always lit from below; NODE, a faceless control-entity that speaks only through its Black Saints, tall enforcers in long black drape whose doctrine is called Mercy, meaning quiet; and CARIBEL, DASH's mother, the Angel Queen of Light, who appears only as overexposure at the edge of frame. The running theme is THE REMEMBERING: when DASH's music lands, a crowd that was standing still wakes up. Everything is original to DASHWORLD - never name or imitate existing anime, games, or their characters.
idle_prompts: DASH drops onto a rain-slick Tokyo rooftop mid-parkour, lands wrong, and the neon in a whole city block dims to match his breathing while EK-0's voice notes the power cost in a flat log entry
A packed crossing of commuters stands perfectly still under the signage; DASH taps one beat into a signal pole and the entire intersection remembers how to move at once, umbrellas rising like a wave
EK-0 assembles itself out of drifting geometry above an empty LIMELYTE dancefloor at dawn and reads a single log entry aloud to nobody, the club lights answering each sentence
TELE tunes her cybernetic arm in a flooded Arca service corridor, testing it by catching a falling wrench three times faster than she should, and does not smile until the fourth
SYLER walks toward DASH down a mirrored Tokyo arcade in inverted color, matching his stride exactly, and every screen they pass shows the other one's face
Two Black Saints in long black drape stand in a bright Arca 250 plaza doing nothing at all, and the crowd around them slowly, politely stops singing
SERAPHINA lights a cigarette from a floor-level lamp in the empty LIMELYTE and tells the room a secret that the camera is deliberately too far away to hear
DASH sits on the edge of an Arca 250 ring with his legs over impossible daylight, headphones on, building a beat out of the sound of the arcology itself breathing
A busted vending machine in a Tokyo alley plays four bars of an old DASH track by accident and three strangers who have never met turn around at the same moment
NODE addresses a plaza through every screen at once in perfect silence, subtitles only, delivering the Mercy Doctrine while a single child keeps humming off-beat
EK-0 replays a corrupted memory of ARCA 250 and the render keeps failing into wireframe, and it narrates the failure with clinical patience until the color comes back
DASH runs a rooftop chase in the rain and every footfall lands exactly on the kick drum until he misses one, and the music and the city both stumble with him
TELE corners a Black Saint in a stairwell and asks it a question; it answers by simply turning its blank face slightly, and she takes that as a yes
The overexposed silhouette of CARIBEL appears at the far end of a Tokyo underpass; DASH does not run toward it, and EK-0 records that he did not
A crowd at an underground LIMELYTE show goes dead quiet on the drop instead of screaming, and every phone light in the room comes on at once without anyone lifting a hand
SYLER performs DASH's own set to an empty Arca amphitheater, note-perfect and completely cold, while the seats fill with black drape one row at a time
DASH teaches a kid in a Tokyo laundromat to hear the rhythm in the machines, and by the last spin cycle the whole room is nodding without noticing
EK-0 tries to compute how long the exile has lasted and returns three different answers, then quietly logs that it has adjusted the model
A LIMELYTE bouncer refuses entry to a Black Saint by simply standing still longer than it does, and the queue behind him starts a slow clap that turns into a beat
DASH awakens a dead Tokyo block — signs, trams, drones, streetlights all coming back in sequence — and then sits down on the curb, drained, as the color holds without him
